experimentName: Partial mental simulation explains fallacies in physical reasoning (Exp 1)
paper-title: Partial mental simulation explains fallacies in physical reasoning
citation: Bass, I., Smith, K. A., Bonawitz, E., & Ullman, T. D. (2021). Partial mental simulation explains fallacies in physical reasoning. Cognitive Neuropsychology, 38(7–8), 413–424. https://doi.org/10.1080/02643294.2022.2083950
description: Participants watch short animations of a gray cannonball and a pink sphere above a grassy field with a hole, then rate the likelihood of various physical outcomes on 0-100 sliders. Each block asks a different probability question (e.g., hit, grass, conjunction, and conditional outcomes) across 15 scenes.
